violations.text: The hand-washing sink downstairs was lacking paper towels. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/27/2026

Molluscan shellfish tags observed without the date of last sale/service. Molluscan shellfish tags must be maintained for 90 days in chronological order and the date when the last shellfish was used from the bag must be noted on the shellfish tag. New Violation. Correct By: 08/27/2026

Thermometer is lacking in the walk-in cooler. All cold holding equipment used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods must have at least one thermometer inside the unit that is located to allow easy viewing of the temperature display. New Violation. Correct By: 08/31/2026

Utensils observed displayed with the lip surface up. Utensils are to be stored so that only the handles are touched by employees and consumers if consumer self-service is provided. In addition, knife observed to be stored between 2 prep units. Utensils must be stored in a clean, dry location. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/27/2026

1-door reach-in and cold drawer unit in the prep kitchen are not in good repair. They are currently not in service. Service has been scheduled. Equipment must be maintained in good repair. New Violation. Correct By: 09/04/2026
The facility is lacking test strips to measure the concentration of the quaternary ammonium sanitizing solution for the 3-bay sink. New Violation. Correct By: 09/04/2026
The facility is lacking thermo labels or similar internal temperature indicating device for the dishwasher. New Violation. Correct By: 09/04/2026

Pasta, which was prepared in advance, was not cooled to 70 degrees Fahrenheit in 2 hours and then to 41 degrees Fahrenheit within 4 hours. Pasta observed with temperature 45 - 46 degrees F in prep unit #1 (hot kitchen). Pasta was made on 8/24 by weekend staff and was placed in a deep pan before it was at 41 degrees F. Proper cooling must be reviewed with all staff. Cooling logs provided and must be maintained. New Violation. Correct By: 08/27/2025

Molluscan shellfish tags must be maintained for 90 days in chronological order and the date when the last shellfish was used from the bag must be noted on the shellfish tag. New Violation. Correct By: 08/14/2025

Food contact surfaces of equipment/utensils (slicer) were observed with an accumulation of food and debris. The food contact surfaces of equipment must be clean to sight and touch. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/14/2025

Pasta, which was prepared in advance, was not cooled to 70 degrees Fahrenheit in 2 hours and then to 41 degrees Fahrenheit within 4 hours. Pasta observed in the hot kitchen prep unit #1 with a temperature of 46 - 52 degrees F. Voluntary disposal during inspection. Proper cooling methods reviewed. New Violation. Correct By: 08/14/2025

Ambient temperature of the salad prep unit in the pantry kitchen was observed held at 45 degrees Fahrenheit. Foods in this unit observed with temperatures of 42 - 43 degrees F. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. TCS foods were moved to properly functioning units. No TCS foods are to be stored in this unit until it is maintaining a consistent temperature at/below 41 degrees F. New Violation. Correct By: 08/14/2025

Establishment ROPs fish products without a HACCP plan. Establishment cannot ROP without approval of RIDOH Center for Food Protection. Establishment is to stop the ROP process and submit a HACCP plan for approval. New Violation. Correct By: 08/14/2025

Shellstock (clams and oysters) located in the pantry kitchen reach-in unit did not have the proper identification tags. Shellstock tags must remain attached to the container in which the shellstock are received until the container is empty. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/21/2024

Shellfish tags must be maintained for 90 days in chronological order and the date when the last shellfish was used from the bag must be noted on the shellfish tag. New Violation. Correct By: 11/21/2024

Food contact surfaces of equipment/utensils (deli slicer) were observed with an accumulation of food and debris. The food contact surfaces of equipment must be clean to sight and touch. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/21/2024

Chowder and soup observed held at 130 degrees Fahrenheit. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be maintained at 135 degrees Fahrenheit or above except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Chowder and soup were reheated to 165 degrees F and returned to hot hold unit. Temperatures must be carefully monitored. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/21/2024

Salad prep unit was observed held at 44 degrees Fahrenheit. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. TCS foods in this unit observed with temperatures of 43 degrees F and were moved to properly functioning units. Service call to be placed. No TCS foods are to be stored in this unit until it is maintaining temperature at/below 41 degrees F. New Violation. Correct By: 11/21/2024

Thermometers are lacking in the some of the refrigeration unit(s). Cold holding equipment used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods must have at least one thermometer that is located to allow easy viewing of the temperature display. Thermometers are to be placed in all cold hold equipment to monitor temperatures. New Violation. Correct By: 11/25/2024

Knives observed stored on an unclean surface (between prep unit and hot hold unit) between uses. During pauses in food preparation, utensils must be stored on a clean surface or in a clean, protected location. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/21/2024

The cutting boards of the prep units are very scratched and scored. Cutting blocks and boards that are subject to scratching and scoring shall be resurfaced if they can no longer be effectively cleaned and sanitized, or discarded if they are not capable of being resurfaced. New Violation. Correct By: 12/15/2024
